newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EMOTIONAL LEMIEUX EXTENDS CAREER, GRETZKY TURNS BACK CLOCK.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EMOTIONAL LEMIEUX EXTENDS CAREER, GRETZKY TURNS BACK CLOCK.

text.p: Mario Lemieux's brilliant career will continue for at least one more game and old Wayne Gretzky was the Gretzky of old as the Pittsburgh Penguins and New York Rangers posted home playoff wins on Wednesday.
The surprising Ottawa Senators also recorded a home victory, knotting their series with the Buffalo Sabres at two games each with a 1-0 overtime win.

With Pittsburgh facing elimination and Lemieux set to retire after this season, Ed Olczyk and Petr Nedved scored short-handed goals in a three-goal first period and Ken Wregget made 37 saves to assure that "Super Mario's" career did not end in a sweep by the rival Philadelphia Flyers.
Lemieux put an exclamation point on the 4-1 victory -- and what may have been his final home game -- by scoring on a breakaway with 64 seconds left.
The Flyers still lead the best-of-seven series three games to one with Game 5 set for Saturday in Philadelphia.

Lemieux sent the emotionally charged Civic Arena crowd into a frenzy when he took a pass from Ian Moran, broke in alone on goaltender Garth Snow and wristed the puck between his pads for his 69th career post-season goal.
"It was perfect, absolutely perfect," Penguins coach Craig Patrick said. "You couldn't write a better script than that. He shed a few tears at the end of the game, he was thrilled."
Moran scored for Pittsburgh 69 seconds into the contest. Shjon Podein scored the lone Philadelphia goal just 36 seconds later to tie the game at 1-1 before it was two minutes old.
But Wregget was perfect the rest of the way.
At the end, Lemieux returned to the ice for a couple of laps around the rink, blowing kisses to the crowd.

"The fans have been there for me through a lot of tough times here in Pittsburgh," Lemieux said. "I was just expressing my feelings toward the crowd. It was just a great moment. When I came off, I started crying."

In New York, the Great One turned back the clock with a vintage Gretzky performance to give the Rangers a three games to one lead over the defending Eastern Conference champion Florida Panthers with a 3-2 victory.
With the Rangers trailing 1-0 after one period, Gretzky took matters into his own hands, scoring a natural hat trick -- three goals in a row -- in the second period.
Gretzky beat Florida goalie John Vanbiesbrouck three times in a 6:23 span -- all on blazing slapshots.
"I haven't had a hat trick in a long time," said the 36-year-old Gretzky after picking up his ninth career playoff hat trick and first since 1993.
The Panthers grabbed a 1-0 lead on Rob Niedermayer's powerplay goal at 13:23 of the first period.
Gretzky tied the game on the power play 3:07 into the second, one-timing a perfect pass from rushing defenceman Brian Leetch past Vanbiesbrouck.
He made it 2-1 at 6:46, finishing off a 2-on-1 break as Luc Robitaille sent a long cross-ice pass to Gretzky, who blasted the puck over Vanbiesbrouck's shoulder into the top of the net.

Gretzky completed the hat trick 2:44 later. He came down the right wing, faked a shot, skated away from the goal while waiting for other players to move into Vanbiesbrouck's line of sight, then fired the puck just inside the far goalpost.
"His shot selection is perfect right now. He looks like the Gretzky of old," Vanbiesbrouck said.
David Nemirovsky brought the Panthers within one, scoring just 1:40 into the third period. But Rangers goalie Mike Richter, who finished with 21 saves, held Florida at bay the rest of the way.
In 197 playoff games, Gretzky has 116 goals and 252 assists for 368 points -- all NHL records.
"What do you say about Wayne Gretzky," said Florida coach Doug MacLean. "There's been 17 years of this, that's why he's the greatest player in the game."
In Ottawa, Daniel Alfredsson broke a scoreless deadlock with the game's lone goal 2:34 into overtime to give the Senators a huge victory over the heavily favoured Sabres.

Alfredsson started the play with a slap shot from just outside the blue line that Buffalo goaltender Steve Shields could not control. Tom Chorske got to the loose puck and left it for Alfredsson, who put a shot past Shields just inside the right goalpost to end the game.
Ottawa goalie Ron Tugnutt faced just 17 Buffalo shots and stopped them all for his first career post-season shutout.
Shields, making his first playoff start in place of injured star Dominik Hasek, was under much greater pressure than Tugnutt. He faced 36 shots, stopping the first 35.
